texts: For CABG and mitral valve replacement in an obese diabetic who has had a long stay in another hospital, the best prophylaxis is a first-generation cephalosporin plus a glycopeptide: cefazolin plus vancomycin.
A long hospital stay raises the chance of colonisation with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, which cefazolin does not cover.
Vancomycin alone is weaker against methicillin-sensitive staphylococci and covers no Gram-negative organisms, so it is added to cefazolin rather than replacing it.
An aminoglycoside is not needed routinely and adds kidney toxicity.
In the picture, the chef and the Van Gogh painter guard the stern together, and the gnome is waved away.
Memory hook: a long stay brings tough grapes: the chef and the painter together.
